title: Paul Graham on handing off YC, founder conflicts, focus, and finding your first 500 true fans
summary: A 2014 fireside chat where Graham explains why he handed YC to Sam Altman, how YC's early model was a summer-job accident, and what he has learned from 632 startups. Key themes: co-founder relationships, brute focus on the one bottleneck, starting with a small intense fire of users, and why determination beats raw intelligence.

principles.text: Pick the single most important thing and do only that; founders already know the answer but don't ask themselves.
principles.quote: the most important thing for startups to do is to focus ah right because there's so many things you could be doing one of them is the most important you should be doing that and not any of the others

principles.text: Start with a small, intense fire: find the few people who want your product a lot and make them extremely happy.
principles.quote: it's impossible to make something that a large number of people want a lot so you've got to find people who want what you're making a lot um and that's necessarily going to be a small number and that's okay

principles.text: Test product-market fit by whether users would be bummed if you stopped, not whether friends say it's good.
principles.quote: just so long as you make Sam feel that he would be bummed if you stopped working on this that's the test right not like your friends say oh yeah it's good I'll use it right

principles.text: Get a co-founder; founders must get along, and the best teams have each founder be king of their own domain.
principles.quote: that's the model that works that's how you have multiple people who are each extremely effective not step on one another's toes

principles.text: Determination and effectiveness beat raw brains; smart but ineffectual founders disappoint.
principles.quote: you can be surprisingly stupid if you're sufficiently determined right

principles.text: Starting a startup is the most efficient route to wealth but is necessarily painful; no pain suggests not trying hard enough.
principles.quote: if it's not a certain amount of painful you're probably not trying hard enough
